sweep_summary: Single works with stress in the title for Vafsi (vafs1240; catalog = set by morphology from Stilo's handout Table One): Bögel, Yousefi & Mirdehghan 2018 (LFG'18, open PDF at CSLI/Stanford) was already held by the project from the 9/16 download and was re-read in full. It is squarely about stress in this language but only at the verbal-complex and clause level: stressed punctual bǽ-, negative nǽ- and preverbs, unstressed durative ær-, stress shift onto a following vowel when æ elides (b-ím-diæ), oblique clitic =om vs stressed full form ím, lexical stress encoded in p-form (Table 6), and unmarked sentence accent on the pre-verbal element (pp. 93-98, 103). This REFINES the catalog's morphological coding (independent, partly acoustic corroboration for morpheme-conditioned stress in verbs, complementing the affix-conditioned nominal facts) but is SILENT on the default word-stress position for nouns, so the catalog's deciding source stands; the 2018 paper is a better the secondary-stress rule citation than the 2021 DOAJ abstract already used by the second reader (same analysis, full English text, open access). Nothing new needs acquiring from this item. Side attempts: Bögel's publications page lists no other Vafsi work beyond the 2019 Konstanz slides (held by the project, same facts); the Yousefi-Mirdehghan-Bögel 2021 Zaban Pazhuhi PDF/landing page (jlr.alzahra.ac.ir) was could not be reached by automated download (automated download 000, direct download failed); written at

new_statements.quote: From the above discussion on the unstressed durative marker, the stressed punctual marker, and the stressed negative marker, it becomes clear why the clitics assume their full form in (9), (8), (10b), and (11): with the durative marker, they have to remain in situ in the initial position of a prosodic phrase, because an adequate host is not available; with the punctual and the negative marker, prosodic inversion is possible, but the stress shift from the markers to the clitic again forces the clitic to assume its full form. Finally, with the preverbs, the clitics undergo prosodic inversion, but are not subjected to a stress shift and can thus retain their clitic form.
new_statements.citation: Bögel, Tina, Saeed Reza Yousefi & Mahinnaz Mirdehghan. 2018. Vafsi oblique pronouns: Stress-related placement patterns. Proceedings of the LFG'18 Conference, 88-108. CSLI Publications.
new_statements.locator: sec. 3.2, p. 98 (summary paragraph after ex. 21); supporting: pp. 95-97 (exx. 14-19, Figs 1-2), pp. 93-94 (sentence stress)
new_statements.reading: Within the Vafsi verbal complex, stress is a property of particular morphemes rather than of a positional count: punctual bǽ-, negative nǽ- and the preverbs are inherently stressed, the durative marker is inherently unstressed, and bǽ-/nǽ- hand their stress to a following vowel-initial element when their æ elides (b-ím-diæ 'I saw'). This is morpheme-conditioned (morphological) stress at the word level, with sentence-level pitch accent handled separately (unmarked: on the element before the verb). The statement is first-hand in the sense that a native-speaker co-author confirmed the data and the paper shows its own pitch tracks, but the descriptive generalizations are credited to Stilo (2004b, 2010). It gives no default position for stress in uninflected nouns, so it does not settle the catalog's open question (expected stem-final default).

audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: both parts of the deciding quotation are verbatim in the copies we hold at the stated loci. The set by morphology classification is defensible on what is held (affix-specific '(unstressed)' vs stressed case suffixes in Stilo's Table One) and is now independently corroborated by an open prosody study downloaded today (Bögel, Yousefi & Mirdehghan 2018, LFG18 pp. 93-97: unstressed durative, stressed punctual bǽ-, stressed negative nǽ-, stressed preverbs, stress-conditioned clitic allomorphy =om/ím, citing Stilo 2004b p. 15). Nothing reached contradicts the classification. sources.quote: The durative marker is unstressed and is therefore unsuitable to function as a host for stranded oblique clitics [p. 95] ... However, in contrast to the durative marker, the punctual marker carries stress. Furthermore, if the element following the punctual marker starts with a vowel, the punctual marker's æ-vowel is dropped and stress shifts to the adjacent vowel: (16) bǽ- (PUNCT) + -av ('come') + -e (3S.DIR) → báwe ('s/he came') (Stilo, 2004b, 15) [p. 96] ... The preverbs are all stressed, i.e., they are suitable hosts for a clitic undergoing prosodic inversion. [p. 98]
sources.note: Full open-access paper, read in full. No general rule for default word-stress position (nouns) is stated; the paper's stress facts are confined to the verbal complex and the clause: (a) inside the verbal complex, stress is carried by specific morphemes — punctual bǽ- and negative nǽ- are stressed, the durative ær-/æt- is unstressed, the preverbs dǽ(r)-, ó(r)-, há(r)- are stressed (pp. 95-98); when bǽ-/nǽ- lose their æ before a vowel, stress shifts to the following vowel (bǽ=om-diæ → b=óm-diæ → b-ím-diæ 'I saw', p. 96), which is why the oblique clitic surfaces in its stressed 'full form' (Stil…
